name: Excerpt: Markdown Web Clipper
summary: Clip any article, or just the text you select, to clean Markdown. Copy it or save a .md file, with optional front matter for Obsidian and other note apps. No access to your sites until you click. Free, no ads, no tracking.
description:
Excerpt turns the page you are reading into clean Markdown: the article without the menus, ads and sidebars, or only the part you selected. Copy it to the clipboard or save it as a .md file, ready for your notes, your docs or an AI chat.

**Clip**
- The readable article of the current page, found with the same engine as Firefox Reader View
- Just your selection: a few words, a code block, some rows of a table or half the page
- The whole visible page, when you want everything
- Headings, nested lists, task lists, links, images, quotes, tables and code blocks with their language come through as proper Markdown
- Also reads what sits inside web components (shadow DOM), which a plain copy of a page misses

**Copy or save**
- A preview you can edit before you copy or save
- Copy to the clipboard, or save a .md file named after the page, with a name that is safe on every system
- Right-click a page or a selection and choose "Clip ... as Markdown", or press Alt+Shift+M: no popup needed (you can change the shortcut in Firefox's "Manage Extension Shortcuts")

**Make it yours**
- Optional front matter with title, source address and date, as a template you can edit: clips drop straight into Obsidian and other note apps as notes with properties
- Heading style, bullet character, links in the text or numbered at the end, images on or off

**Free, for real**
Every feature is unlocked for everyone. No ads, no account, no analytics. Everything happens in your browser; nothing you clip is sent anywhere.

If Excerpt saves you time and you'd like to say thanks, there's a Ko-fi link in the popup. It's entirely optional and unlocks nothing.

**Permissions**
Excerpt asks for no access to your websites when you install it. It can read a page only at the moment you click its button, its menu entry or its shortcut there.

**Good to know**
- Firefox doesn't let add-ons work on its own pages (about: pages, addons.mozilla.org, the built-in PDF viewer, Reader View), so Excerpt can't clip there
- Images are not downloaded: the Markdown links to the picture on the web
- Desktop Firefox only for now. Firefox for Android has no right-click menu and no keyboard shortcuts for add-ons, and Excerpt has not been tested there yet
- Open source inside, unchanged: Mozilla Readability (Apache License 2.0) and Turndown (MIT License)
